new_statements.quote: En el caso del idioma Achi, de acuerdo a este análisis se caracteriza en tener un acento fijo, es decir, una misma palabra no puede tener mas de un significado dependiendo el acento [...] Caso d: Otro caso de palabras acentuadas en el idioma Achi se puede notar que el acento cae en la última sílaba, es decir las que se conocen como agudas. [...] Caso e: Algunas palabras del idioma Castellano han pasado a formar parte del léxico del idioma Achi, ya han adquirido el acento de éste idioma ya que en el habla de las personas el acento se marca en la última sílaba.
new_statements.translation: In the case of the Achi language, according to this analysis it is characterized by having a fixed accent, that is, one and the same word cannot have more than one meaning depending on the accent [...] Case d: Another case of accented words in the Achi language: it can be noted that the accent falls on the last syllable, that is, the words known as oxytones (agudas). [...] Case e: Some words of the Spanish language have come to form part of the Achi lexicon; they have already acquired the accent of this language, since in people's speech the accent is marked on the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Xitumul Toj, Norma Telma. 2003. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Achi. Rabinal, Baja Verapaz: Comunidad Lingüística Achi / Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala (K'ulb'il Yol Twitz Paxil).
new_statements.locator: Capítulo I Fonología, section 'El acento', pp. 52-54 (PDF pages 52-54 of 200; quote from pp. 52 and 54)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: born-digital Word-2013 PDF, 200 pp., text layer) re-extracted with extracted text. All three quoted sentences are present verbatim: p. 52 "En el caso del idioma Achi, de acuerdo a este análisis se caracteriza en tener un acento fijo, es decir, una misma palabra no puede tener mas de un significado dependiendo el acento, sin embargo puede tener mas de un significado pero de acuerdo al contexto en que se ubica."; p. 53 "Caso d: Otro caso de palabras acentuadas en el idioma Achi se puede notar que el acento cae en la última sílaba, es decir las que se conocen como agudas."; p. 54 "Caso e: Algunas palabras del idioma Castellano han pasado a formar parte del léxico del idioma Achi, ya han adquir…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is fixed and non-contrastive and falls on the final syllable of the word (examples for Cubulco: [toka:n] 'blackberry', [sanik] 'ant', [kunbal] 'medicine', [xoron] 'cold'; loans [meSa] 'table', [kape] 'coffee' are re-stressed finally). Departures are morphologically conditioned: clause-final intransitive imperatives in -oq are final-stressed, but clause-medially the suffix becomes -a and stress moves to the penult; superlative adjectives in -alaj take initial stress in Rabinal/San Miguel/Salamá/San Jerónimo (not in Cubulco, where laj is a separate word); adjective+noun compounds with an epenthetic vowel keep an accent on the adjective root plus the final accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such. The source says adjective+noun compounds 'permiten el acento en dos sílabas de la misma palabra' (one on the adjective root: first syllable if monosyllabic, otherwise the syllable before the epenthetic vowel; the other on the last syllable), e.g. [ráxkiná'] 'green bean', [nímawináq] 'elder'; examples are given only for the non-Cubulco varieties.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) intransitive imperatives: final stress with -oq clause-finally, penultimate stress with -a clause-medially (both Cubulco and the other varieties); (b) superlative -alaj adjectives stressed on the first syllable, explicitly 'no se cumple' in Cubulco; (c) compounds with two accents; (e) Spanish loans adopt final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('una misma palabra'), phonemic-analysis based, impressionistic transcription with acute accents; the imperative case shows sensitivity to clause-final vs clause-medial position. The grammar takes the Cubulco municipal variant as the base and tabulates Cubulco forms in a separate column next to Rabinal/San Miguel Chicaj/Salamá/San Jerónimo, stating that variation between municipalities is minimal.
new_statements.identity_note: achi1258 is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping entry for Cubulco Achi' (ISO [acc]); ISO CR 2008-048 (England, adopted 2009-01-16) merged it into Achi [acr] = Glottolog achi1256 as a dialect. The statement quoted is from an ALMG descriptive grammar of Achi as a whole that takes the Cubulco municipal variant as its base and tabulates Cubulco forms in a separate column beside Rabinal/San Miguel Chicaj/Salamá/San Jerónimo (Rabinal Achi' = the other bookkeeping entry, achi1257). If achi1256 is already in the catalog, this record should be merged into it rather than counted as a separate language.

sources.note: Section 'El acento' pp. 52-54: Achi has fixed (non-contrastive) accent; words are stressed on the last syllable ('agudas'); Spanish loans take final stress because 'el acento se marca en la última sílaba'; exceptions: clause-medial intransitive imperatives (suffix -a) take penultimate stress, superlative -alaj adjectives take initial stress (not in Cubulco), adjective+noun compounds carry two accents. Cubulco forms are tabulated in their own column.
